subject: Archaeology
title: The First Medical Texts
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The First Medical Texts.

hook.text: Babylonian doctors kept medical records on clay tablets — case notes, prescriptions, and even surgical instructions.

buildup.text: The Diagnostic Handbook from 1000 BCE lists symptoms head-to-toe and gives treatments for each condition.

discovery.text: Many remedies used real medicinal plants — some overlap with modern pharmacology. Others invoked demons and spells.

twist.text: Doctors were legally accountable. Hammurabi's Code said if a surgeon killed a patient with a bronze knife, his hand was cut off.

climax.text: Babylonian medicine combined observation, herbalism, and religion — not so different from medieval European medicine.

punchline.text: They mixed herbs with spells and held surgeons legally accountable.

quiz.question: What legal consequence did Babylonian surgeons face under Hammurabi's Code?
options: They had to pay the patient's family double the medical fee
A surgeon who killed a patient could lose his hand
They were banished from the city for one year
